newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran moves political rally at Moslem pilgrimage.
newsitem.headline: Iran moves political rally at Moslem pilgrimage.

text.p: Iran on Saturday postponed a controversial political rally it planned to hold next week at the Moslem haj pilgrimage to avoid confrontation with Saudi authorities, state-run Tehran Radio said.
It said the decision was taken after Saudi forces were deployed in front of the Iranian haj offices in Mecca to prevent the rally, called the "disavowal of infidels".

Iran's senior haj official Mohammad Mohammadi Reyshahri in a statement read on the radio criticised the Saudi action, saying the Mecca rally was postponed "to avoid giving Saudi officers an excuse to defile the divine shrine (Kaaba)".
He said Iranian pilgrims would hold the rally in nearby Mena or Mount Arafat but did not say when.
Reyshahri had said on Friday that the rally to denounce the United States and Israel would be held in Mecca on Monday.
Saudi authorities have banned all political activities during the haj which reaches its climax next week.
Saudi Arabia on Wednesday urged Iranian pilgrims to refrain from holding the rally which has been an issue straining ties between the two Gulf powers for years.

Radical Shi'ite Iran says Moslems should air their political grievances during the haj, mainly through rallies to denounce Israel and the United States as enemies of Islam. Sunni Saudi Arabia says the pilgrimage is purely religious and should not be politicised.

The row between the Gulf's two richest oil states over the rallies has resurfaced at every haj since 1987, when 402 people, mostly Iranians, died in clashes with Saudi security forces at an Iranian-led rally. Iran boycotted the haj for three years.
Saudi Arabia has said it would deal harshly with violators of the ban on political activity during haj.
To avoid confrontation with Saudi security, Iranian pilgrims in recent years staged low-key rallies within Iran's haj compounds and Saudi forces did not interfere.
About two million Moslems, half of them from outside Saudi Arabia, are expected to perform this year's haj at Mecca, site of Islam's holiest shrine.
